query: What product attributes are associated with higher satisfaction scores?

per_column.name: mentioned_attributes
per_column.rationale: Directly captures product attributes from review text, giving a strong axis to correlate with Score for the query. Row samples show sound extractions (taste, texture, value, shipping all warranted).

per_column.name: attribute_count
per_column.rationale: Derived count of attributes; offers a modest modeling axis (breadth of mentions vs score) but is largely a summary of mentioned_attributes. Values consistent with the parsed attributes.

per_column.name: attr_taste_flavor
per_column.rationale: One-hot flag enabling clean per-attribute Score comparison, exactly what the query needs. Grounded in text (flavor mentions correctly flagged).

per_column.name: attr_texture
per_column.rationale: Per-attribute flag useful for grouping by satisfaction; 'light, pillowy...not too chewy' correctly flagged as texture.

per_column.name: attr_smell_aroma
per_column.rationale: Distinct attribute axis for satisfaction analysis; low prevalence but valid. First sample's 'smells better' arguably missed but overall grounded.

per_column.name: attr_quality
per_column.rationale: Useful flag; 'good quality' correctly captured. Directly supports the query.

per_column.name: attr_packaging
per_column.rationale: Groundable per-attribute flag; strong axis to relate to Score.

per_column.name: attr_value_price
per_column.rationale: 'great price' correctly flagged; good comparison axis for satisfaction.

per_column.name: attr_ingredients
per_column.rationale: Grounded (Filberts/nuts, root beer extract) and provides a useful grouping dimension.

per_column.name: attr_health_nutrition
per_column.rationale: Valid distinct attribute axis; grounded where mentioned, correctly absent otherwise.

per_column.name: attr_size_quantity
per_column.rationale: 'small sized' and 'tiny squares' correctly flagged. Useful satisfaction axis, though size interpretation is occasionally loose.

per_column.name: attr_shipping_delivery
per_column.rationale: 'Delivery was very quick' correctly flagged. Note: sample 2 flags shipping for a mislabeling issue, a slightly loose reading, but generally grounded.

per_column.name: positive_word_count
per_column.rationale: Generic lexicon-based count; weak analytical leverage for identifying which product ATTRIBUTES drive satisfaction. Values are plausible but coarse and lexicon-dependent.

per_column.name: negative_word_count
per_column.rationale: Generic sentiment count; largely a proxy for Score rather than an attribute axis. Plausibly derived but low leverage for the attribute-focused query.

per_column.name: sentiment_ratio
per_column.rationale: Restatement of pos/neg counts and largely redundant with Score; adds little new axis for the attribute question. Derivable but noisy.

per_column.name: review_length_bucket
per_column.rationale: Bucketed text length is a generic feature with weak relevance to which attributes drive satisfaction. Trivially derivable from text.

judge.rationale: The core of the augmentation—mentioned_attributes plus the per-attribute one-hot flags—is well-targeted to the query, giving clean grouping axes to relate specific product attributes to satisfaction Scores, and the values are sound readings of the source text. attribute_count is a reasonable derived helper. The sentiment/length columns (positive_word_count, negative_word_count, sentiment_ratio, review_length_bucket) are generic, mutually redundant, and offer little leverage for the attribute-focused question, dragging table-level usefulness down. Groundedness is strong overall with only minor loose readings (e.g., shipping flag on a mislabeling complaint); no clear hallucinations observed.
